notes.approach: Push the middle rock along the corridor and keep moving right until Baba reaches the flag.
notes.mechanics: BABA IS YOU chooses the controllable object. ROCK IS PUSH makes rocks movable, and touching the flag wins because FLAG IS WIN.
notes.attempts: One successful attempt. This introductory level is included in the fresh run.

notes.approach: Push IS out of WALL IS STOP to leave the lower room. Reassemble FLAG IS WIN upstairs, then reach the flag.
notes.mechanics: Rules change as soon as their words move. Without STOP, walls can be crossed. Keep the finished rule clear of the route to the goal.
notes.attempts: One successful attempt. I moved the entire lower wall rule out of the way while routing the words.

notes.approach: Control the wall, push STOP out of FLAG IS STOP, and bring WIN down to replace it. Touch one of the now-winning flags.
notes.mechanics: YOU can apply to a wall as easily as to Baba. The same flag objects can change from obstacles into goals.
notes.attempts: One successful attempt. An input command was split during tool use; I checked the board and continued from that position.

notes.approach: Sacrifice one rock to clear a water tile at the exit. Replace PUSH with WIN in the rock rule, then return to touch the remaining rock.
notes.mechanics: SINK consumes both the water tile and an overlapping object. The visible flag need not be the final goal: another noun can become WIN.
notes.attempts: The first attempt pushed WIN against the bottom wall. I restarted and approached it from below using the open right-hand column. The failed attempt and restart remain in the recording.

notes.approach: Arrange three rocks in a row and push them into the skull enclosure. The leading rock displaces SKULL in SKULL IS DEFEAT while Baba remains outside. Then walk to the flag.
notes.mechanics: A chain of pushable objects extends the reach of a push. DEFEAT harms the controlled character, so ordinary rocks can cross the skull boundary.
notes.attempts: One successful attempt. I first checked the upper edge while looking for access to the fixed rules, then assembled the rock chain.

notes.approach: Shift BABA IS YOU left as a complete sentence to exit the chamber. Reuse IS and PUSH to form LAVA IS PUSH, then push a path through the river to the flag.
notes.mechanics: A hot hazard can also be pushable. With PUSH active, the lava moves away before Baba overlaps it, allowing MELT to remain in place.
notes.attempts: One successful attempt. The chamber exit and immovable rule blocks took substantial inspection; those idle thinking gaps are shortened.

notes.approach: Break WALL IS STOP, then push WALL into the BABA IS YOU sentence as BABA moves aside. Move the controlled walls right three and down two to bring one into the flag.
notes.mechanics: A new noun can replace an old noun in a single push, transferring control immediately. When many objects are YOU, keep distant copies from disturbing the controlling sentence.
notes.attempts: One successful attempt. I paused after the control transfer to choose a wall movement that would leave WALL IS YOU intact.

notes.approach: Place FLAG above the IS in BABA IS YOU and WIN below it. Route the words around the visible enclosure; its walls have no STOP property.
notes.mechanics: One IS can serve two crossing rules. For a push route, check the square behind the word as carefully as the destination, especially near STOP grass.
notes.attempts: I misread dark grass tiles and tried two dead-end WIN routes. The recording retains the failed moves and all undo sequences. A closer grid inspection exposed the open column needed for the successful lower route.

notes.approach: Push SINK out of BABA IS YOU AND SINK. Move that spare word into the bottom jellyfish; both disappear, leaving an opening to the flag.
notes.mechanics: Text is an object and can be sacrificed to SINK. The blue patterned ground has no STOP rule here; the fixed blocking rule applies to WALL.
notes.attempts: An initial whole-sentence push was blocked by a wall. I then reached the exposed SINK word from above and detached it directly before making the opening.

notes.approach: Give the star both SINK and PUSH, then push it into the skull. Reuse AND to extend BABA IS YOU into CRAB AND BABA IS YOU, and walk the outside crab to the flag.
notes.mechanics: AND can join properties or nouns. Once the star has removed the skull, its conjunction is free for the control rule. Store movable words with a usable route back out.
notes.attempts: The first exit route hit a wall and later inputs moved the wrong words. I restarted, checked intermediate positions, and completed the two-stage plan. The full failed attempt and restart remain visible.

notes.approach: Replace PUSH in LOVE IS PUSH with MOVE from KEKE IS MOVE. Walk below the algae enclosure and wait for the moving heart to reach Baba.
notes.mechanics: MOVE advances on each turn, including Space waits. The heart keeps its vertical direction and crosses DEFEAT algae safely because it is not YOU.
notes.attempts: I first watched the heart from the side, then moved below its vertical route and waited. All gameplay waits remain; the automatic replay entered after completion is excluded.

notes.approach: Line up two pillars and push the front one through the star boundary. Route PILLAR around the wall enclosure and replace BABA in BABA IS YOU, then move the pillar inside to the flag.
notes.mechanics: DEFEAT only threatens objects that are YOU. A push chain can deliver an ordinary object across a hazard; transferring control afterward lets that object act inside the enclosure.
notes.attempts: I checked the upper boundary while examining the fixed rules, then used the pillar chain and switched control. The exploratory moves are retained.

notes.approach: Use the BABA in BABA IS YOU as the top of a vertical BABA IS WIN. Move the spare IS up and left, then move WIN left and up beneath it.
notes.mechanics: An object that is both YOU and WIN wins immediately. A shared noun can begin two crossing rules, so reaching the enclosed flag is unnecessary.
notes.attempts: The recorded assembly worked without an undo or restart. The long planning pause is removed; all moves remain.

notes.approach: Spend the two keys on the first two doors. Bring ROCK outside and form ROCK IS KEY to create a third key. Reuse that IS to restore KEY IS PUSH, then push the new key into the final door.
notes.mechanics: OPEN and SHUT remove one another. A noun transformation persists after its rule is broken, while PUSH needs an active rule. This lets one IS serve two successive purposes.
notes.attempts: A routing detour pushed PUSH to the bottom edge. I undid 17 moves, repositioned ROCK, and completed the transformation. The detour and every undo remain visible.

notes.approach: Share one IS between horizontal KEY IS OPEN and vertical KEY IS PUSH, then open the first door. Reuse the horizontal KEY noun to replace SHUT in DOOR IS SHUT. Push the resulting key aside and reach the flag.
notes.mechanics: Crossing rules can share their IS. A spare noun becomes useful again once its first rule has served its purpose, and changing a door into a key removes the door’s STOP property.
notes.attempts: The crossing-rule assembly and door transformation worked without an undo or restart. Every movement is preserved; only long inactive planning gaps are removed.

notes.approach: Replace STOP in WALL IS STOP with JELLY, removing JELLY from its own STOP rule. Walk through the transformed boundary, then build a vertical BABA IS WIN beneath BABA IS YOU.
notes.mechanics: Removing STOP alone would leave WALL IS DEFEAT dangerous. Changing the wall noun removes that hazard. Two adjacent IS words can be pushed as a chain while preserving BABA IS YOU.
notes.attempts: Some setup moves shifted the spare IS and STOP farther than intended; I continued from that position. No undo or restart was needed. The area-clear animation is retained.

notes.approach: Shift the upper ROCK IS ROCK sentence out from under the wall and break it. Rearrange the lower words into ROCK IS FLAG, then touch the restored flag.
notes.mechanics: I treated ROCK IS ROCK as an identity constraint and removed it before attempting a different transformation. The resulting ROCK IS FLAG successfully changed the object back into a winning flag.
notes.attempts: The planned rearrangement worked without an undo or restart. All moves are retained; inactive thinking time is removed.

notes.approach: Add IS SHUT beside the fixed KEY noun. The key is already OPEN, so it disappears and clears the passage to FLAG IS WIN. Replace KEKE with DOOR in the control rule, then move the door onto the flag.
notes.mechanics: One object that is both OPEN and SHUT destroys itself. A blocked passage can be cleared by changing the obstructing object’s properties, and control can transfer by replacing a rule noun in one push.
notes.attempts: The planned sequence worked without an undo or restart. IS had to be placed before SHUT because the hedges restrict access to their final positions.

notes.approach: Build JELLY IS BABA above the fixed BABA noun to create a controllable Baba beyond the wall. Use that Baba to move FLAG from FLAG IS STOP into the lower JELLY IS WIN sentence, then reach the flag.
notes.mechanics: A transformation into an already controlled noun creates another YOU object. FLAG IS FLAG visibly blocks FLAG IS JELLY. Multiple Baba objects move together, but walls can stop one while the other keeps moving.
notes.attempts: The first control shortcut was blocked by a wall, the flag passage jammed, and FLAG IS JELLY was rejected. I inspected the rules, found the Baba transformation, and recovered from a misplaced FLAG. All attempts remain; no restart was needed.

notes.approach: Give the pushable flag OPEN and use it to open the side room. Build BABA IS BABA, then push CRAB through the upper passage until CRAB IS WIN forms. Walk to the crab.
notes.mechanics: A noun’s identity rule blocks competing transformations. BABA IS BABA protects control when moving CRAB temporarily creates BABA IS CRAB. The flag substitutes for Baba as the object consumed by OPEN and SHUT.
notes.attempts: The full sequence worked without an undo or restart. I checked the identity rule before pushing CRAB through the transformation and defeat rows.

notes.approach: Give walls SHUT and the pushable star OPEN. Use the star to remove a wall tile, leave the room, and break KEY IS DEFEAT. Bring IS and WIN inside to make KEY IS WIN, then touch the key.
notes.mechanics: OPEN and SHUT work on walls as well as doors. An object can make an opening while Baba stays safe, and reaching outside rules can change a previously lethal object into the goal.
notes.attempts: The first setup trapped the star beneath the wall rule, so I restarted. I also corrected the IS and OPEN alignment after the KEY word blocked a push. The failed setup, restart, corrections, and successful route are all retained.

notes.approach: Turn the rock into a second Baba. Move one Baba into the flag chamber while the crabs are harmless, then use the other to shift the upper nouns and activate FLAG IS WIN.
notes.mechanics: ROCK IS BABA creates another controlled object. Walls can hold one Baba still while the other moves, letting an object pass a future hazard before its DEFEAT rule becomes active.
notes.attempts: The first rule shift made the flag WIN but blocked access with DEFEAT crabs. I undid that push, built the second-Baba setup, and completed the staged solution. The initial attempt and undo remain.

notes.approach: Temporarily control the rock to extract it. Restore Baba, share an IS between BABA IS YOU and ROCK IS PUSH, and use the freed IS as a second crate. Push the rock through the crab, then transfer control to the rock inside the goal chamber.
notes.mechanics: Text can serve as a pushable object in a chain. Sharing rule words can free a crate without losing an essential property. Temporary control lets a trapped object move itself into a useful position.
notes.attempts: The first push made the flag WIN but the crab DEFEAT. I developed the extraction and crate route from that position, temporarily parking PUSH to clear the text route. All 243 inputs remain, with no restart or undo; long planning pauses are removed.

notes.approach: Shift the IS stack down while preserving the lower rules. Move VIOLET aside and temporarily lift ROSE out. Insert a spare IS between ROSE and FLAG, then restore ROSE to create winning flags outside the wall.
notes.mechanics: Identical IS words can replace one another without breaking an active sentence. A shared noun can participate in both a transformation and a winning rule, creating reachable goals elsewhere.
notes.attempts: The spare IS initially went one square too far. I undid five moves and corrected its placement. Every move and undo is retained; the long planning pause is removed.

notes.approach: Shift BABA IS YOU left to make room below its noun. Route ROCK around the enclosure and replace BABA, then move the grounded rocks right to the flag.
notes.mechanics: FLOAT does not let Baba pass STOP walls. Transferring control to grounded rocks puts the controlled objects at the same height as the winning flag.
notes.attempts: I first tested upward movement against the wall, then used the control transfer. No undo or restart was needed; all moves remain.

notes.approach: Remove AND FLOAT from Baba and place it after WATER IS HOT. Walk grounded Baba beneath the floating hot water and floating skulls to the grounded flag.
notes.mechanics: HOT/MELT and DEFEAT interactions require matching height. Changing the hazard’s height can be more useful than changing Baba’s height, especially when the goal remains grounded.
notes.attempts: The rule transfer worked without an undo or restart. Every movement is retained, with inactive planning time removed.

notes.approach: Push the lower rock into the first water tile. Build ROCK IS YOU vertically using the YOU already in BABA IS YOU, walk the trapped upper rock out, and sink it into the second tile. Baba then crosses to the flag.
notes.mechanics: A controlled object can leave a corner that makes it impossible to push. Two YOU rules allow Baba to stay safe while the rock moves into the water; walls block their movement independently. Floating text cannot sink grounded water.
notes.attempts: I initially tried to get above the upper rock, but a hedge blocked the needed square. The control rule solved that obstruction. All blocked moves remain; no undo or restart was used.

notes.approach: Break ROCK IS PUSH, then push the spare PUSH and IS words into adjacent water tiles. Cross the resulting gap to the flag.
notes.mechanics: ROCK IS FLOAT keeps the rocks above the water, so they cannot sink it. Text has no FLOAT rule in this version and can be sacrificed instead. BABA IS YOU remains intact throughout.
notes.attempts: My initial route pushed a rock down and displaced PUSH. I recovered the word from its new position and completed the crossing. No undo or restart was needed; the extra movements remain in the recording.

notes.approach: Use the cogs to clear the side water tiles. Push TEXT IS FLOAT as one intact sentence across the spring; its front word pushes WIN out onto dry ground. Move WIN below BABA, break the floating sentence, and reuse its IS to form BABA IS WIN.
notes.mechanics: Moving a whole sentence can preserve its rule while its words act as a long pushing chain. The central water tile was hidden beneath WIN. Removing TEXT IS FLOAT too early sinks both that word and its water tile.
notes.attempts: Two crossings failed, and an early attempt to reuse FLOAT destroyed WIN. Both deaths and the full undo sequence are retained. I also tested the top boundary before finding the intact-sentence approach; no restart was used.

notes.approach: Push BABA against the left wall to stagger the robots, then move it up to the top-left corner. Align the robots side by side and sacrifice the leading one to open the top water tile. Bring IS and YOU back across that opening to complete BABA IS YOU; Baba reaches the flag.
notes.mechanics: A word blocked by a wall can stop one controlled object while another keeps moving. This creates the offset needed to sacrifice only one robot. The rule can be assembled on the noun’s side of the river rather than carrying the noun across.
notes.attempts: The planned offset and word return worked without an undo or restart. The deliberate blocked movements used to align the robots are retained.

notes.approach: Move Baba’s control sentence below the thief’s route. Stop the robot inside the left pocket and make ROBOT IS YOU share YOU with BABA IS YOU. Use both characters to bring WIN out, then keep the robot controlled while assembling BABA IS WIN. The robot touches Baba to finish.
notes.mechanics: A MOVE object can push a control word away. Sharing YOU allows two characters to cooperate, and the winning object can be different from the controlled object. The isolated pipe pieces block several tempting routes around WIN.
notes.attempts: The recording keeps the stolen control word, a fatal skull step, three restarts, and the undo sequences used to recover rule routing and an overshot WIN push. Inert waits did not create distinct undo states, which also caused a rollback farther than expected. The Area Clear animation is retained.

notes.approach: Control the flag temporarily and use the same IS for KEY IS BABA, creating a second Baba. Restore BABA IS YOU AND OPEN, sacrifice one Baba to open the inner water tile, and retrieve WIN with the survivor. Slide the control sentence upward, remove OPEN, and insert WIN.
notes.mechanics: A perpendicular transformation can create another copy of the original player while a different noun remains controlled. OPEN and SHUT destroy both participants, so an extra controlled object is needed. The pond’s narrow entrance makes the standing square behind WIN crucial.
notes.attempts: The first route trapped WIN in the corner. A direct OPEN test destroyed Baba, followed by a restart. One undo repaired a control-word push during the flag phase. All experiments, blocked moves, and the successful two-Baba route remain.

notes.approach: Stage the bolt facing away from the dangerous corridor, then activate MOVE. Push DEFEAT into the skull rule before the bolt reaches the hot skull. The bolt’s pushing chain removes SKULL from that rule, opening the lower route. Retrieve WIN, make BOLT IS WIN, and touch the bolt.
notes.mechanics: A wall reversal buys time for a remotely moving object. The bolt is MELT, so HOT must be removed before it reaches a skull. A non-YOU mover can then pass DEFEAT and push a rule that Baba cannot safely reach.
notes.attempts: The first bolt route displaced PUSH and required rebuilding its rule. Later, an attempted WIN insertion shifted the whole sentence; I rerouted WIN above the property slot. All moves remain, with no undo or restart.

notes.approach: Send the cog across the bog and stop it beyond the upper rule slot. The robot delivers AND against that stopper and returns. Reuse the cog-rule words in a three-word train; the far wall stops the train with IS between ROCK and WIN. Touch the local flag once FLAG AND ROCK IS WIN is complete.
notes.mechanics: A remotely positioned STOP object can set the destination of a pushed word. A fixed wall can do the same for a longer word train. FLAG IS FLAG blocks transformations but does not prevent FLAG from gaining WIN through an AND sentence.
notes.attempts: Several routes displaced spare words and required rearranging the local rules. The cog was stopped at its intended position, and both deliveries succeeded. No undo or restart was used; every extra move remains.

notes.approach: Make Keke pushable and park it above the wall-rule column. Remove PUSH, slide the column upward so WALL overlaps Keke, and transfer control to Keke. From inside that word, push IS and STOP down to break the rule. Reuse IS and the outside WIN word to make BABA IS WIN, then touch Baba.
notes.mechanics: An object without PUSH can share a cell with a text word. Giving that object YOU lets it move from inside a sentence, pushing a word that was otherwise inaccessible. Once WALL IS STOP breaks, the prison boundary can be crossed.
notes.attempts: Direct wall-rule pushes and pushing Keke against the wall failed. A control-word routing mistake led to one restart. The successful overlap setup and all earlier attempts are retained; no undo was used.

notes.approach: Use KEKE IS BABA to create a second Baba. The stepped wall lets one Baba wait above WALL IS STOP while the other pushes the column upward over it. Move down from inside WALL to break the sentence. Retrieve IS and WIN and form BABA IS WIN.
notes.mechanics: Multiple YOU objects can be positioned independently when different walls block them. One can hold still while another pushes text onto it, giving access from inside a rule without needing PUSH.
notes.attempts: The first alignment pushed the wall column downward and merged the Babas. Nine undos restored the setup, and a left sidestep kept the lower Baba clear of the column. All movement and the corrected solution are retained; no restart was used.

notes.approach: Send a stopping cog across the bog to park the first AND. Send two spare words as spacers, then deliver the second AND against them. Finally, let the robot push the complete ROBOT IS MOVE sentence, plus a final spacer, into the last row. The moving sentence stays active until its IS completes FLAG AND ROCK AND ICE IS WIN.
notes.mechanics: A mover can push the very sentence that grants it MOVE. An intact sentence keeps working as it slides. Remote stoppers and word spacers determine where each delivery ends. FLAG IS FLAG still allows FLAG IS WIN.
notes.attempts: Several routing errors required rearranging the words again. I pushed the robot against the top edge and used 14 undos to recover, then stepped into the bog and undid that death. No restart; every input, failed route, wait, and undo remains in the video.

notes.approach: Control both floating rocks and line them up one tile apart. Cross below the flag rule, then push its IS and WIN back across the river. Bring those words to the original ROCK noun so horizontal ROCK IS WIN crosses vertical ROCK IS YOU.
notes.mechanics: Floating text can be carried across SINK water. A noun can anchor two perpendicular sentences, letting the same rocks be YOU and WIN without needing an AND.
notes.attempts: My first plan tried to turn the rocks into grounded Babas, but the hedge boxed in the required rule. I restarted once. During the successful attempt, WIN was pushed too far down and recovered from below. All inputs and both attempts are preserved.

notes.approach: Add AND YOU to the existing BABA IS MELT sentence at the bottom. That frees the IS from the original control rule. Use it with the fixed WATER noun and the spare FLOAT word to make WATER IS FLOAT, then cross to the flag as grounded Baba.
notes.mechanics: One YOU can finish two rules, allowing the original rule to be dismantled safely. WATER IS WATER prevents transformations but still permits FLOAT. Floating HOT water and DEFEAT skulls do not interact with grounded Baba.
notes.attempts: An early route pushed the control column to the top edge and then displaced YOU. Fourteen undos restored the setup. The completed route retains those errors and the recovery; no restart was used.

notes.approach: Remove WEAK from Baba. Make SKULL IS WEAK and push a rock through two skulls to open a passage. Reuse the same IS and WEAK beneath the lower ROCK noun, keeping ROCK IS PUSH active. Push the exit rock against a wall so it breaks, then reach the flag.
notes.mechanics: A weak object breaks on overlap; a weak pushable object also breaks when its push is blocked. One noun can anchor perpendicular property rules when the original property cannot be replaced.
notes.attempts: Walking straight into the hedge destroyed weak Baba, recovered with one undo. Later, replacing PUSH was blocked by the wall above it, so I built the second rule instead. All failed pushes, routing corrections, and the successful exit are retained; no restart.

notes.approach: Let moving Baba sink and leave a rock through BABA HAS ROCK. Reuse HAS and ROCK beneath the fixed ROCK noun to make ROCK HAS ROCK. Push the rock through the water: every sink opens a tile and creates a replacement rock, letting Keke follow to the flag.
notes.mechanics: HAS creates the named object when its owner is destroyed. ROCK HAS ROCK makes a renewable pushable object, while each SINK water tile is consumed only once.
notes.attempts: The setup and crossing worked without an undo or restart. The recording retains all waits while Baba moved, the complete word-routing sequence, and every push across the water.

notes.approach: Transfer control to the box, cross the hot water, and break LOVE IS MELT outside. Restore heart control and BOX IS PUSH. Position the box in hot water before adding a perpendicular BOX IS MELT sentence; BOX HAS FLAG then releases the flag for the heart to reach.
notes.mechanics: A controlled box can cross HOT water while it lacks MELT. Removing the heart’s MELT makes the same crossing safe for it. HAS turns destruction into a way to create the goal, and a shared noun can keep PUSH active while adding MELT.
notes.attempts: The controlled box pushed spare words during its excursion, so I retrieved and rearranged them. The PUSH column was shifted temporarily to make room for the final box push, then restored. Every movement and correction is retained; no undo or restart.

notes.approach: Turn the box into a second Keke. Sacrifice one Keke to open the word chamber, then use its BOX word to prepare KEKE IS BOX. A single push forms that transformation and BOX IS YOU together. Reuse HAS and the second BOX for BOX HAS BOX, then cross the river as a continuously replaced box.
notes.mechanics: Transformation can create another controllable character without triggering HAS. Identical IS words can replace one another without breaking control. A noun replacement can simultaneously form a new control rule and a transformation.
notes.attempts: The staged transformations, chamber entry, and self-replacing crossing worked without an undo or restart. The sacrificed Keke, every rule movement, and all water crossings remain in the recording.

notes.approach: Build a chain of controlled replacements: Baba breaks on rubble and leaves a box; the weak box leaves a key. Before opening the door, arrange KEY HAS BOX and keep BOX IS YOU active so the destroyed key leaves a playable box inside the room.
notes.mechanics: HAS takes effect when an object is destroyed. A noun pushed out of one sentence can complete another in the same move, changing control and WEAK together. The rubble ring has an empty center, so the handoff must happen on an actual rubble tile.
notes.attempts: The first box-to-key handoff failed because the box stood in the empty center of the rubble ring. One undo restored it; moving the setup down one tile made the replacement work. All word routing, the failed handoff, and the final extra step to the flag are retained.

notes.approach: Build BOX HAS KEY AND BOX across the top row. Share its first BOX with IS PUSH and its last BOX with IS WEAK. Break the box against the first door, then move IS and PUSH underneath KEY. Push the generated keys through both doors; the replacement box supplies another key when Baba overlaps it. Restore LOVE IS WIN and touch the heart.
notes.mechanics: HAS can produce two objects with AND, including another copy of its owner. A weak box can therefore leave both a key and a replacement box. Sharing nouns between perpendicular rules makes the compact top-row layout possible, and the pushable property can be transferred to the generated keys.
notes.attempts: Several word-routing errors required 41 undos, including an IS stranded at the bottom, a PUSH collision, and pushing the box toward the wrong wall. The final approach displaced IS from LOVE IS WIN; I recovered it without restarting. Every failed move and correction remains, followed by the third-flower area-clear animation.

notes.approach: Line up two ghosts with IS and PUSH on adjacent rows. Activate GHOST IS MOVE and stop it when the payloads form SKULL IS PUSH beneath the remote SKULL noun. Push through the barrier, break SKULL IS DEFEAT, and remove PUSH from the skulls. Retrieve WIN and make GHOST IS WIN, then touch a carrier.
notes.mechanics: Two synchronized movers can deliver a vertical rule across a lethal barrier while the player stays behind. A dangerous object becomes safely pushable when it also has PUSH. Removing a mover rule can allow one final step, which must be included in delivery timing.
notes.attempts: Two restarts retain the initial direction experiment and a word-routing error. A later attempt moved PUSH too early, leaving the second ghost behind; I restored PUSH, aligned the carrier, and recovered without another restart. A brief reactivation of MOVE during the final WIN placement advanced the ghosts one extra tile, so the final approach needed one more step.

notes.approach: Stage Keke facing the door. KEKE IS MOVE carries it across the first moat, and KEKE HAS BABA leaves a second controlled Baba when the door consumes Keke. Keep that Baba safe while reversing the contents to BABA HAS KEKE. Send it into the second moat, let the resulting moving Keke reach dry land, then replace BABA with KEKE in the control sentence and reach the flag.
notes.mechanics: DEFEAT affects controlled characters; an autonomous mover can cross it. HAS transfers an object across destruction by a door or hazard. With two YOU objects, wall positions and horizontal separation determine which word-routing moves are safe. Remove HAS from the control-noun swap path to avoid a gap in control.
notes.attempts: The first launch pushed the BABA word apart, so I moved the whole rule assembly below the travel lane. Another rollback widened the spacing between the two Babas. All 34 undos and failed moves remain. A small planner, built only from the observed board, checked the final shared-movement routes against walls, words, and lethal water; no restart.

notes.approach: Push the lower sentence right to make WALL IS ROCK and escape. Place one rock above the ice enclosure, then prepare perpendicular ROCK IS WALL and ROCK IS BABA rules that activate together. The rocks become overlapping walls and controlled Babas. Two upper Babas move the spare IS into WALL IS WIN while another Baba stays inside a corner wall.
notes.mechanics: Two simultaneous noun transformations create both named objects on each original tile. A controlled character already overlapping a STOP object can remain there when adjacent walls block its movement. Keeping the final sequence to right and down preserves the overlap needed for WIN.
notes.attempts: No undo or restart. I opened a second passage in the rock ring to retrieve WIN, then staged every word before transforming. The final sequence was two rights, down, two rights. A local single-object routing tool avoided moving unrelated words and kept the transformation trigger cell forbidden until the setup was ready.

notes.approach: Stage three right-facing Babas to carry three rows. The upper row keeps KEKE IS PUSH active; the middle carries BABA IS MOVE itself; the lower pushes Keke and YOU. Move YOU out of alignment before crossing, then wait while Keke is transported without being controlled. The far-side obstacles stop the rows at different positions and restore KEKE IS YOU. Walk down to the flag.
notes.mechanics: An autonomous mover can carry the complete sentence that grants MOVE. A pushable character can cross DEFEAT while YOU is temporarily inactive, and autonomous moves continue during waits. Different fixed stopping positions can align a control sentence after a crossing.
notes.attempts: No undo or restart. One Baba initially reached the left edge facing outward; a brief MOVE pulse let it bounce back before I restored PUSH and staged it. All repositioning and the ten waits during the uncontrolled crossing remain. The final alignment restored control at the predicted safe position.

notes.approach: Replace SHIFT with PUSH and extract one belt from the bridge. Push it under the dangerous gate, then restore SHIFT to move the wall off that tile. Alternate PUSH and SHIFT to advance the same belt twice more, moving the blocking wall far enough aside to leave a passage. Disable SHIFT before crossing and walk around the relocated wall to the flag.
notes.mechanics: SHIFT moves objects standing on a conveyor even when those objects are not pushable. DEFEAT affects the controlled character, so a pushable belt can safely overlap the dangerous wall. Turn off the conveyor before walking over it if its direction would carry YOU into a hazard.
notes.attempts: No undo or restart. The bridge belts were pushed into the upper pocket so one could be extracted from above. Three wall shifts opened the route, and the final crossing used the inactive belt. All positioning, property swaps, and waits remain.

notes.approach: Bring SHUT and IS inside to make the walls shut. Give the key both PUSH and OPEN, then spend it on the floor beneath the trapped PUSH word. Use that word to make WALL IS PUSH, open the enclosure around WIN, and bring WIN back to a sentence sharing BABA with the control rule.
notes.mechanics: SHUT by itself does not block movement. A key can remove one shut wall and expose an otherwise trapped rule word. Once walls are pushable, whole columns can be shifted to open passages, but those walls can also push text and accidentally break a rule.
notes.attempts: One undo, no restart. Placing IS beside BABA initially pushed a wall into the control noun and removed YOU; the following ineffective inputs remain. Undo restored control, then moving the wall column cleared the sentence. All 271 inputs, including the failed route and recovery, are preserved.

notes.approach: Transform both doors into trees and push the entrance tree into the skull corridor. Build TREE HAS TREE and TREE IS SINK, with PUSH removed, so each collision consumes a skull and leaves a replacement tree. Once the patrol is gone, remove SINK and walk through the harmless trees to the flag.
notes.mechanics: A pushable object can block a collision that SINK needs: removing PUSH lets the moving skulls overlap the trap. HAS recreates the tree after each destruction, turning one object into a renewable trap. Noun transformations persist after their sentence is dismantled.
notes.attempts: 21 undos, no restart, 303 inputs. The first trap consumed only one skull; undo restored it while the self-replacement rule was prepared. Several word-routing mistakes and the waits for both trials remain. The observed-board routing tool helped recover the words near the entrance wall.

notes.approach: Borrow the belt rule’s IS and SHIFT to give Baba SHIFT. Walk onto the inactive belt to move it to the canyon exit, then push the hot ghost onto it. Rebuild BELT IS UP to orient the relocated belt and replace UP with SHIFT to lift the ghost into the open room. Push the ghost through the melting flowers and follow it to the flag.
notes.mechanics: A controlled character with SHIFT can move a non-pushable object by walking onto it. Moving the belt also changes its facing, so set its direction after positioning. UP fixes direction; it does not cause movement, and that facing persists after UP is removed. Floating text does not get carried by grounded Baba’s SHIFT.
notes.attempts: One restart, no undo, 404 inputs. Early attempts tried inaccessible routes and tested floating text against a hedge. Later routing mistakes pushed UP against the right wall; moving the belt sentence beside that stranded word recovered the setup. Every route, failed move, reset, and direction test remains.

notes.approach: Use short MOVE runs and temporary RIGHT or UP rules to steer Keke around the right chamber. Wall bounces turn those directions into leftward and downward travel. Push WIN down into the lower passage, circle Keke behind it, and send the word left through the flowers. Build KEKE IS WIN and touch the returned courier.
notes.mechanics: Direction properties set facing, which persists after the rule is removed. Remove the forced direction before relying on a wall bounce. MOVE starts on the following input and breaking it permits one final step, so the stopping move belongs in the count. An uncontrolled courier crosses DEFEAT safely.
notes.attempts: One restart and one undo, 282 inputs. An early routing error pushed the wrong words and led Baba into a flower. The rebuilt setup used verified stopping points beside WIN and at each turn. All steering, waits, the failed setup, and the final delivery remain.

notes.approach: Teleport the PUSH word across the river and replace TELE with it. Push the right heart onto the water tile above the flag. Rebuild LOVE IS TELE for one activation, moving that water tile onto the distant heart, then break the rule. Walk through the newly dry gap to the flag.
notes.mechanics: TELE transports other objects overlapping a teleporter, including hazardous water. Turning TELE off after the transfer preserves the new arrangement. A transported word can block the destination and be pushed aside when Baba arrives, so check the landing position.
notes.attempts: One restart and two undos, 114 inputs. The first route stranded PUSH near the river. Later, accidentally stepping back onto a heart returned Baba to the wrong side and caused a death. An incomplete rule restoration caused another failed crossing; the successful attempt visibly moved the water away before entering the gap. All attempts remain.

notes.approach: Push the left heart under the PUSH slot, displacing the word and turning that property off. Send PUSH through the hearts and teleport Baba to the far side. The word now alternates between hearts, so wait between pushes to guide the hot heart through the water. Push the word off the heart to stop the cycle, teleport back to the opened entrance, and walk to the flag.
notes.mechanics: TELE exchanges overlapping words every input. Aligning a teleporter with a rule slot makes a property turn on and off on alternate turns. Waiting lets the next push occur while PUSH is active. HOT removes the water before Baba follows the heart into its former tile.
notes.attempts: One restart, no undo, 48 inputs. The initial attempt pushed a heart into the rock barrier; the exchanged rocks left a lethal tile behind and Baba died. The successful attempt used the alternating rule and cleared two water tiles so PUSH could be removed sideways without blocking the flag corridor. All moves and waits remain.

notes.approach: Use the ice teleporters to move the lower Baba into the key chamber, then replace ICE IS TELE with BABA IS TELE. Align the two controlled Babas so the lower one carries the key onto the upper one. Step away to leave it there, restore KEY IS PUSH, and push it through the door to the flag.
notes.mechanics: TELE moves other objects overlapping its subject. Giving it to YOU turns a controlled character into a movable teleporter. Both Babas obey every direction, so walls and backed-up words provide the unequal movement needed to align them.
notes.attempts: One undo, no restart, 104 inputs. An early word placement accidentally formed BABA IS ICE and removed control. After undoing, moving ICE out of the shared column allowed the intended rule. Routes came from a small planner using only a manually transcribed view of the board; every actual move remains.

notes.approach: Slide LEAF IS DEFEAT left to expose an empty cell beside the sentence. Make the ghosts pushable and place one in that cell. Restore TELE, then slide the sentence over the ghost to send its IS to the lower ghost. Restore PUSH at the right moment and deliver the spare IS between LOVE and WIN. Walk through the now harmless leaves to the heart.
notes.mechanics: A non-pushable teleporter can sit beneath text. Moving the sentence over it extracts a word that cannot be reached from above. Overlapping words exchange on every input, so include the route back to the property switch when choosing when to stop TELE.
notes.attempts: Two undos, no restart, 148 inputs. An early route displaced the ghost noun and the control sentence; the undos recovered them. The recording also retains an accidental entry into Telephone and the return to the map before Haunt. All word swaps, waits, and positioning moves remain.

notes.approach: Share the IS in BABA IS YOU with a vertical FENCE IS NOT STOP sentence. Walk through the opened boundary and retrieve the outside IS and WIN. Place them beneath BABA to add BABA IS WIN while keeping control.
notes.mechanics: A negated property overrides its positive version: FENCE IS NOT STOP disables the fixed FENCE IS STOP rule. A noun can anchor two perpendicular sentences, preserving YOU while adding the winning property.
notes.attempts: No restart or undo, 105 inputs. One short positioning detour approached the fence noun from the wrong column before correcting it. All movements and the rule inspection remain.

notes.approach: Open the fence with FENCE IS NOT STOP, sharing the IS in BABA IS YOU. Bring the outside WIN inside before closing the boundary. Move NOT above FENCE and put WIN below the shared IS, forming NOT FENCE IS WIN. Baba satisfies that subject while retaining YOU.
notes.mechanics: NOT before a property removes that property; NOT before a noun selects objects other than that noun. Sharing IS between perpendicular rules preserves control while changing which objects can win.
notes.attempts: Five undos, no restart, 129 inputs. Lifting NOT too close to BABA briefly formed NOT BABA IS YOU and changed control. After undoing, routing NOT through a farther-left column avoided the accidental sentence. All movements and recovery remain.

notes.approach: Arrange all four crates in a horizontal pull chain between Baba and the flag. Push WIN left while pulling the entire chain: the same input takes the flag off its water tile and changes the bricks from HOT to DEFEAT. Pull the flag clear of the bricks, park the crates away from the approach row, and break AND PULL so Baba can touch the flag.
notes.mechanics: PULL propagates through a continuous chain. Combining that movement with a word push can rescue an object in the very input that changes its hazards. PULL also blocks direct entry, so remove it from the winning object before touching it. Crates behind a turn can follow into an unintended tile.
notes.attempts: Both recorded sessions are joined, preserving 218 inputs. The early rule shift melted the flag. Later gaps in the crate chain repeated that failure, and crates following Baba into the rule alcove trapped the exit. Undos recovered the flag and the approach. Blocked moves and changes of facing also appeared in undo history; all attempts remain.

notes.approach: Use RIGHT to ferry BELT and IS across the conveyor and retrieve UP. Stage the rock below the upper rule and a spare direction word beside it as a stopper. Rebuild BELT IS UP at the left entrance, then ride the conveyor while the rock rises toward IS. The rock completes FLAG IS WIN after Baba has entered the enclosure.
notes.mechanics: Belts retain their facing after the direction rule breaks. SHIFT advances a carried object once per input, while a character walking with the belt can advance twice. That difference lets Baba enter before the rock turns the belts into walls. A word backed by a wall can hold the rock on the correct conveyor lane.
notes.attempts: All 214 inputs are retained. An early route displaced BELT, the retrieval overshot UP, and the first entrance setup sent UP along the wrong conveyor lane. Undos repaired those arrangements before the successful timed ascent.

notes.approach: Make Baba PULL and the ghost MOVE. Pull the ghost into position facing right, then let it carry Baba across the passage on wait inputs while the upper flag stays still. Step away from the ghost, retrieve FLAG, and bring the word back below the working rules to complete FLAG IS WIN.
notes.mechanics: An autonomous moving object can pull a PULL object, including one that is also YOU. Wait inputs separate that movement from the other controlled object. A weak winning ghost breaks before contact can win, in either direction. The returning ghost eventually pushes MOVE out of its own rule and stops.
notes.attempts: All 297 inputs and three restarts remain. Failed approaches tried touching a winning ghost, making it move into Baba, and using BABA IS MOVE for independent travel. A supposed recess for parking the flag was blocked. The successful ghost ferry preserved the flag and allowed precise one-tile movement around the FLAG word.

notes.approach: Use the rock to clear the foliage, then make LEAF both PUSH and TELE. Arrange PUSH on the left leaf so restoring the rule teleports Baba to the right with PUSH active. Push the right leaf under the key, then alternate pushes and waits to carry the key through the teleporter pair. Deliver it above the ghost and push the ghost into the key.
notes.mechanics: A pushable teleporter moves away when approached, so enter it in the same input that activates PUSH. Floating text stays on its leaf while grounded objects teleport. Move the leaf only while the key is on the other side; a wait resets that timing. OPEN removes the SHUT ghost, whose HAS rule releases the winning flag.
notes.attempts: Both recorded sessions are joined, preserving all 320 inputs and 54 undos. Earlier rock placement and a trapped PUSH rule were recovered with undo. The first session confirmed that floating text could not be teleported. The successful route uses the detour around the isolated hedge in the upper-right room.

notes.approach: Use LOVE IS TELE to move a river tile onto the other heart. Switch back to PUSH and move the heart out of the dry opening, then bring both hearts and the movable rules to the left bank. Place one heart on the water above the flag. Use the PUSH word as a buffer to move the other heart off its water, teleport the flag’s blocking water away, and break TELE before it returns.
notes.mechanics: Teleporters carry water and text as well as Baba. Breaking TELE freezes the transported water in its current place. A chain of words can keep a rule active while being pushed across the river. A word in front of Baba can push a heart off a dangerous water tile while Baba stays one cell back on dry ground.
notes.attempts: All 385 inputs, two restarts, and 33 undos remain. Earlier attempts tested swapping PUSH and TELE through the hearts and timed transport of PUSH alongside the water. The successful attempt made a permanent river opening first, then used a buffered push and a one-input teleport to open the flag’s approach.

notes.approach: Prepare the key first: extract it with MOVE, carry it around the right side with PULL, and aim it downward in the central opening. Park it against the lower hedge. Then aim a leaf the same way and give it MOVE. It bounces upward, reaches the fungus, and pulls it down into the safe opening. Switch MOVE from the leaf to the key to open the fungus, then pull the leaf sideways and reach the released flag.
notes.mechanics: A moving object can pull a PULL object behind it. The lower hedge reverses a downward mover, allowing it to travel up through foliage while Baba stays outside. The key must be positioned before the fungus blocks the aiming square. OPEN removes the SHUT fungus, and FUNGUS HAS FLAG leaves the winning flag behind.
notes.attempts: All three recorded attempts are joined: 1,338 inputs, 17 undos, and two restarts remain. The first setup moved the fungus before preparing the key. Later mistakes included stepping into leaves, pushing spare words while crossing their rows, and overshooting rule positions. The successful attempt prepared the key first, then used a timed noun swap and a final sideways pull.

notes.approach: Temporarily made Keke pullable and dragged it sideways. Restored the key’s PULL rule and Keke’s MOVE rule, letting Keke reverse against the key and tow it across the river. Stopped Keke on the left bank, then pulled the key around the wall and into the box to release the flag.
notes.mechanics: Pulling changes a mover’s facing. Autonomous MOVE can tow a PULL object through water that defeats the player. OPEN and SHUT destroy the key and box; HAS releases the flag. SHUT alone did not prevent Baba from standing on the box.
notes.attempts: Three retained visits include unsuccessful word-extraction and lower-river routes, waits, undos and a restart. The final visit tested Keke’s movement axis, then switched between PULL and MOVE to complete the ferry. All original attempts are joined; only idle thinking gaps are removed.

notes.approach: Switched between ROCK IS PUSH and NOT ROCK IS PUSH to clear selected pond tiles with the two rocks and push the remaining water aside. Brought NOT down the dry passage, then prefixed the lower clause before shifting it right to open the flag corridor.
notes.mechanics: NOT ROCK IS PUSH makes water and plants pushable while HEDGE IS NOT PUSH preserves the walls. Pushable water can be moved onto an inert rock to remove both. NOT BABA IS NOT YOU leaves Baba controlled while the obstructing sentence is moved.
notes.attempts: Three retained visits include insufficient rock routes, water and plant experiments, restarts, failed inputs and undos. The successful visit used displaced water to open a route for the second rock, then cleared the NOT delivery path. Every input is retained; only idle thinking gaps are removed.

notes.approach: Brought the rock and TEXT into the lower chamber. Put TEXT below the final WALL in WALL IS WALL and used the rock as a buffer for one last upward push. WALL IS TEXT replaced the identity rule, turning the walls into words and opening a path to the flag.
notes.mechanics: Uncontrolled text and a pushable rock can enter a DEFEAT wall safely. The rock keeps Me off the wall during the final push. Replacing the identity rule allows WALL IS TEXT to transform the walls; FLAG IS WIN remains intact.
notes.attempts: All three visits are retained. Earlier TEXT IS YOU movement destroyed the winning rule, and a separate buffer experiment pushed the rock outside without freeing Me. The final visit rearranged the buffer to replace the identity rule, with a failed wall step and its undo preserved.

notes.approach: Made KEKE IS BABA first, creating a second controlled Baba in the sealed chamber. Reused the words to make TEXT IS HOT and melt the ghost with a two-word buffer. Then TEXT IS WEAK let Baba destroy the skull rule and clear the passage. One Baba completed FLAG IS WIN; the other reached the flag.
notes.mechanics: A transformation persists after its rule is broken. Two YOU objects move together but can be positioned differently using walls. Hot text melts a MELT ghost; a buffer keeps the player off DEFEAT. Weak text can be destroyed against a wall, allowing the skull hazard rule to be removed safely.
notes.attempts: Both visits are retained. The first melted the ghost but stranded the KEKE word, then tested an irreversible WEAK-first setup. The successful return transformed Keke before sacrificing its noun. A route planner based on the observed board helped keep both Babas alive; every route was checked in the game, and a buffer-positioning undo is preserved.

notes.approach: Changed control to TEXT IS YOU, then used the right wall to align BABA IS PUSH through the same IS. Repositioned the cross-shaped rule and pushed Baba through the top skull. The PUSH word was destroyed, while the control rule stayed above the barrier. Shifted the remaining words against the left wall to restore BABA IS YOU, then walked to the flag.
notes.mechanics: DEFEAT affects YOU objects, so an uncontrolled, pushable Baba can cross the skulls. A controlled carrier word can be sacrificed after pushing Baba clear. Walls stop some words while others keep moving, allowing a shared IS to switch rules and restore control.
notes.attempts: One recorded visit. The first alignment pushed Baba too far upward; four undos restored it and a wider route avoided contact with YOU. All positioning moves, failed inputs, undos and the successful crossing are retained; only idle thinking gaps are removed.

notes.approach: Aligned IS WIN in the upper room, created two boxes, and transported one through the water. Used wall stops to place it precisely before IS WIN while the other box restored Keke control. BOX IS TEXT created the winning rule. Then TEXT IS YOU and a wall-clamped KEKE IS BOX created a physical winning box; a final wall-assisted switch to BOX IS YOU completed the level.
notes.mechanics: Floating text does not teleport, so a physical box carries its future noun into the room. Transformations persist after their rule is broken. Walls can stop different parts of a controlled text arrangement, allowing a shared IS to create a box and then switch control to it. An object that is both YOU and WIN wins immediately.
notes.attempts: All five visits are retained. Earlier attempts tested text teleportation, created an upper word in the wrong position, and confirmed FLOAT does not bypass STOP walls. The final visit fixed the delivery position, tested a direct Keke-to-box transformation that lost control, and solved the return to BOX control with a staged text arrangement. Positioning mistakes, failed inputs and undos remain. During visit two the game closed and capture ended before 19 subsequent logged inputs (about six seconds). Those original input logs are retained, but no video exists for that interval; no replacement footage was fabricated.

notes.approach: Completed WATER IS SINK with the WATER word on the river. The word and that water tile disappeared, leaving a crossing while preserving IS and SINK. Reused them for COG IS SINK, brought the cog through the gap, and sank the leftmost skull. Baba could then push FLAG directly into FLAG IS WIN and return to the flag.
notes.mechanics: A rule can remove one of its own words when that word overlaps a newly active SINK object. The water gap remains after the rule breaks. A SINK cog removes a skull through overlap, but does not pass a STOP wall. Removing the skull nearest FLAG avoids the need for a long push buffer.
notes.attempts: All four visits are retained. Earlier attempts explored river crossings and word buffers, and tested a SINK cog against a blocked word. The final visit also tested a STOP wall, then solved the resource shortage by sacrificing WATER itself. A routing error and its undos are preserved, along with all other inputs and waits.

notes.approach: Placed the loose NOT before the fixed NOT PUSH to form BOX IS NOT NOT PUSH. With the boxes now pushable, the flag sank one into the outer water layer, aligned the second with that gap, and used it to remove the inner layer. The flag then walked to Me.
notes.mechanics: Two NOT modifiers cancel: the game interprets BOX IS NOT NOT PUSH as BOX IS PUSH. A pushed box and one SINK water tile disappear together, so two boxes can open a single path through two water layers while the flag remains controlled.
notes.attempts: All five visits are retained. Earlier attempts explored control through NOT FLAG IS YOU, sacrificed boxes into adjacent water tiles, and tested NOT BOX IS NOT PUSH without gaining box pushability. The final visit tested double negation on the property instead, confirmed BOX IS PUSH in the rules menu, and solved the crossing. Earlier mistakes and undos remain.

notes.approach: Used TEXT HAS BABA to turn a KEKE word sacrificed in the upper pond into a second Baba. Reversed the rule to BABA HAS TEXT, then sacrificed one Baba in the lower water. Its BABA word completed BABA IS FLOAT. The survivor crossed the upper pond and skull to form FLAG IS WIN, then moved FLOAT aside before touching the flag.
notes.mechanics: HAS can turn a destroyed word into a controlled object, then turn that object back into its noun. Sharing BABA between the HAS and YOU rules preserves control while changing the death result. FLOAT avoids ground-level SINK, but also prevents contact with a ground-level winning flag; push the lower rule down and move FLOAT sideways to return to the ground.
notes.attempts: All three visits are retained. Earlier visits tested TEXT IS YOU, created Keke from a sunk IS, and explored word duplication without a usable control transfer. The final visit first tried the lower-IS sacrifice, undid it, and used the upper word instead. A route-model error caused a lost Baba and was undone; a missing fence segment was corrected after live inspection. All mistakes, failed inputs and undos remain.

notes.approach: Created a second Baba by sinking KEKE under TEXT HAS BABA. Separated the two Babas at the fence corner, then pushed TEXT onto one trapped against the fence as BABA HAS TEXT became active. Its BABA word overlapped TEXT. Moved that stack above HAS BABA to form BABA HAS BABA while preserving BABA IS YOU. The survivor crossed the water and skull, assembled FLAG IS WIN, and returned to the flag.
notes.mechanics: A word can defeat Baba while simultaneously completing the rule that determines its contents. Overlapping BABA and TEXT can share a sentence position. Using the stack as the subject creates BABA HAS BABA and TEXT HAS BABA without BABA HAS TEXT, so defeated Baba reappears without leaving obstructing words. A fence corner separates simultaneous YOU objects.
notes.attempts: Both visits are retained. The first created two Babas but did not produce a usable self-containment rule. The final visit proved the word-crush interaction against the left wall, restarted because the stacked words were trapped there, and rebuilt beside the inner fence. Several positioning attempts preceded the successful separation and rule reversal. All recorded inputs, mistakes, waits and restarts remain.

notes.approach: Moved the controlled boxes together, then restored BOX HAS KEY. Pushed loose text into the weak boxes to create controlled keys on the far side of the bugs. Used those keys to extend BUG IS DEFEAT with AND WEAK, opened a gap in the bug line, and crossed the five doors to reach the flag.
notes.mechanics: WEAK boxes release their HAS contents when text overlaps them. The new keys obey KEY IS YOU. With BUG IS DEFEAT AND WEAK, a key destroys a bug and survives the contact. Overlapping keys can open successive SHUT doors, consuming one key for each door.
notes.attempts: All eleven visits are retained, including the inspection-only fourth part. Earlier attempts tested wall collisions during HAS changes, bent noun lists, transformations and KEY HAS BOX without crossing the barrier. Text collisions later produced keys on the right, but the return route remained blocked. The final visit reused that setup and added WEAK to the bug rule. All mistakes, failed inputs, waits, restarts and undos remain.

notes.approach: Made the flags pushable and moved the upper flag into the stone corridor. Restored teleportation, then sent an upward-facing Keke through the upper flag. KEKE IS SHIFT moved the lower flag upward. Pushed WIN onto the upper teleporter, retrieved it below, and completed FLAG IS WIN before touching a flag.
notes.mechanics: The gray stones have no STOP rule and can be crossed. Switching PUSH between Keke and the flags allows their positions to be set. TELE carries objects and words between flags; SHIFT lets Keke move an overlapping flag in its facing direction. Raising the lower teleporter leaves room to recover the arriving WIN word.
notes.attempts: Completed in one visit without undo or restart. Several blocked moves and miscounted routes were corrected in place, and waits tested teleport timing. The successful setup moved both flags before sending WIN through. All failed inputs, positioning moves and waits remain.

notes.approach: Gave the same rock both BABA and KEY transformations, creating an extra Baba and a key. Made the key pushable and used it to open the door. Sent both Babas through, sacrificed one to remove a water tile, then guided the survivor through the gap to the flag.
notes.mechanics: Simultaneous ROCK IS BABA and ROCK IS KEY rules produce both objects from one rock. A pushable OPEN key opens the SHUT door and is consumed. WATER IS SINK consumes one Baba and one water tile, leaving a gap for the other Baba.
notes.attempts: The first branch turned the only rock into a key and opened the door, then recognized that one Baba could not cross the surrounding water. Seventeen undos restored the setup before the dual transformation. During later word routing, a temporary KEY IS YOU rule moved the key down one tile; its route was adjusted. All inputs, positioning mistakes and undos remain; there was no restart.

notes.approach: Placed the loose IS and EMPTY below the fixed BELT word to form BELT IS EMPTY. The conveyors disappeared, leaving a clear route to the flag.
notes.mechanics: Using EMPTY as the transformation target removes the belts. The new vertical rule shares BELT with the fixed BELT IS SHIFT sentence; no belts remain to push Baba away from the flag.
notes.attempts: Solved on the first visit without undo, restart or death. The recording also retains a brief code inspection of the completed Skull House level and the navigation into Rocket Trip. All actual inputs remain.

notes.approach: Used DOOR IS EMPTY to remove the doors, then reused IS and EMPTY beside the existing BABA IS YOU rule to form EMPTY IS BABA. This created Babas throughout the empty spaces, including inside the flag room. Moved down and left to reach the flag.
notes.mechanics: EMPTY can be the subject as well as the result of a transformation. EMPTY IS BABA creates Baba in unoccupied cells, and the new Babas obey BABA IS YOU. Their simultaneous movement can push rule words, so the direction chosen after activation matters.
notes.attempts: One visit, two undos and no restart. The first right move after creating the Babas broke the control rule; the following down input could not move them. Two undos returned to before activation. Reactivated the rule, then moved down and left to win. All failed inputs and the undo sequence remain.

notes.approach: Used ROCK IS EMPTY to remove the rock above the wall, letting EMPTY IS BABA create Babas there. Stopped the growing group, sent the upper Babas around the wall, and brought WIN back to complete ICE IS WIN. Moved a Baba onto the ice to finish.
notes.mechanics: ROCK IS NOT BABA prevents a direct rock-to-Baba transformation. Removing the rock makes room for EMPTY IS BABA to create a Baba instead. Empty starting spaces keep producing Babas as earlier ones move away. BABA IS STOP makes the Babas block one another, so the positions of several Babas matter when moving words.
notes.attempts: Completed in one visit without undo or restart. The growing group required changes to the EMPTY rule and several positioning corrections. The Babas pushed ICE and IS down against the wall, and pushed WIN left before lifting it into the rule. All inputs and incidental word shifts remain.

notes.approach: Switched to EMPTY IS YOU and used empty spaces to move the rocket out of the entrance and reposition the control words. Held IS and YOU against the clouds while moving BABA back above them. With BABA IS YOU restored, walked through the open entrance to the flag.
notes.mechanics: EMPTY IS YOU can push objects and words from empty spaces, while an occupied source cell prevents that push. EMPTY control could not touch the winning flag directly. The clouds stopped selected words so the BABA control rule could be restored.
notes.attempts: Completed in one visit without undo or restart. Tested EMPTY control and its blocked pushes, then moved the rule above the cloud and used a down/up sequence to align BABA for the final switch. All actual inputs and positioning moves remain.

notes.approach: Used two loose words to bridge the key from its cloud pillar onto BABA IS YOU. Reused those words to complete KEY IS OPEN, then slid the intact control sentence beneath the key. Pushed the key across the moving text platform into the door and walked to the flag.
notes.mechanics: PUSH text supports the falling key; Baba without STOP does not. Moving all three words of BABA IS YOU together preserves control. Alternating a full-row push with a key push advances the key while keeping text directly below it.
notes.attempts: Completed in one visit with two undos and no restart. The support test let the key fall past Baba to the floor; two undos restored the staged words. Five verified bridge cycles then carried the key to the door. The failed fall, both undos and all positioning moves remain.
